quarterly_data.signal: GF was selected as the technology provider and operator for two new semiconductor fabs at its Malta, New York site under a U.S.-Japan initiative providing up to $21 billion in funding: Japan provides the investment, GF contributes its technologies, manufacturing expertise and operations. An initial investment of approximately $10 billion will accelerate construction of a new 300mm fab expected to come online in 2029, adding approximately 900,000 300mm wafers of annual U.S. manufacturing capacity when fully operational; an additional investment of approximately $10 billion would fund a second fab adding approximately the same amount. GF expects to break ground on the first fab at the permitted, shovel-ready Malta site later this year; the capacity targets automotive, industrial and connected infrastructure markets. CEO Tim Breen: GF was selected because 'fabs of this scale require more than capital. They require differentiated technology, operational excellence and a proven ability to execute.'
quarterly_data.figure: up to $21 billion initiative; first fab approximately $10 billion, online in 2029, approximately 900,000 300mm wafers a year; second fab approximately $10 billion

quarterly_data.signal: GF agreed with the U.S. Department of Commerce to amend its existing CHIPS and Science Act award to reallocate $955 million and accelerate its investments in silicon photonics, silicon-germanium (SiGe) and advanced packaging at its facilities in Malta, New York, and Burlington, Vermont, expanding domestic manufacturing capacity for communications-infrastructure and data-center technologies.
quarterly_data.figure: $955 million CHIPS award reallocated to silicon photonics, SiGe and advanced packaging

quarterly_data.signal: Customers and a supplier quoted in GF's release on the new Malta capacity: Apple COO Sabih Khan said Apple has partnered with GlobalFoundries to produce essential chips for Apple products in the United States, with GF an inaugural member of Apple's American Manufacturing Program; Cirrus Logic CEO John Forsyth said the new fabs give Cirrus Logic access to domestic manufacturing capability for next-generation mixed-signal products, building on its long-standing relationship with GF; GM president Mark Reuss said GM and GF established the first direct automaker-to-foundry supply agreement; Tokyo Electron CEO Tony Kawai said Tokyo Electron has supported GF's manufacturing operations across its global sites for many years.

connects_to.relationship: GF foundry (FDX, BCD, feature CMOS + integrated NVM) manufacturing Renesas SoCs / power devices / MCUs under a multibillion-dollar strategic partnership

contracts.signal: Renesas CEO Hidetoshi Shibata, quoted in GF's release on its two new Malta, New York fabs: Renesas is planning around GF's new capacity in New York as an extension of Renesas' own production footprint, an expanded collaboration that strengthens the stable, long-term supply of semiconductors its products require.
